Q1: Copper(I) iodide exhibits several officially recognized significant hazards (Tier 1) for environmental, oral, dermal/eye, and organ/systemic health. It also shows potential carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive, and inhalation hazards based on a broader range of scientific data (Tier 2). Information regarding its endocrine disruption potential is currently data deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: Copper(I) iodide is not identified on any lists of concern. It is, however, recognized on the EPA's "Substances Added to Food" inventory and FDA's "GRAS list," indicating it is generally considered safe for specific applications, particularly as a food additive under regulated conditions.
Q3: Copper(I) iodide is extensively characterized, evidenced by its specific molecular formula (CuI) and classification as a "Small Molecule" with a well-defined structure. It is also well-studied, with 22,000 literature references, significantly exceeding the median for the comparison chemical set, and has only one data-deficient hazard class (EDC).
